summary: Appends a node a2 to the tail of a doubly-linked list. First unlinks a2 from any list it currently belongs to (DoublyLinkedListNodeUnlink), then zeroes a2's next/prev link slots. If the list head at this+0x14 is non-null, walks from it following each node's next pointer at +0x64 to find the tail, then splices a2 in: updates the tail pointer at this+0x18, links the old tail's next to a2, and sets a2's prev link. If the list is empty, sets both head (this+0x14) and tail (this+0x18) to a2. Does nothing if a2 is null.

local_names.v3: tail-find traversal cursor; also list head when empty
local_names.i: walked node used to advance toward the tail

operations.description: If a2 is null, return immediately without modifying the list.
Unlink a2 from any list it currently belongs to before re-appending.
Zero a2's next pointer (offset 100, 0x64) and prev pointer (offset 104, 0x68) so it is a standalone node.
Read the list head pointer from this+0x14 (this[5]) into v3.
If the head v3 is non-null, walk to the tail; otherwise the list is empty.
Walk from the head node toward the tail by repeatedly reading each node's next pointer at +0x64 until the next pointer is null, leaving v3 on the last node.
Splice a2 at the tail: set the list tail pointer this+0x18 to a2, set the old tail's next pointer at +0x64 to a2, and set a2's prev pointer (offset 104, 0x68) back to the old tail v3.
Empty-list case: set both the head pointer this+0x14 and the tail pointer this+0x18 to a2.
